frontier_candidates.title: Dynamic Human Gate Optimization
frontier_candidates.core_hypothesis: Introducing a dynamic optimization algorithm for human gate placements will enhance the quality of generated research papers by strategically timing human interventions.
frontier_candidates.why_now: Current human interventions are static and may not align with the most impactful moments in the research process; dynamic optimization could lead to better outcomes.
frontier_candidates.claim_it_tests: The effectiveness of human intervention timing on paper quality metrics.
frontier_candidates.minimal_experiment: Conduct a controlled study comparing static vs. dynamically optimized human gate placements across multiple research tasks.
frontier_candidates.benchmark_or_evaluator: Custom evaluation metric based on expert ratings of paper quality.
frontier_candidates.human_taste_role: Human experts will provide feedback on the timing and relevance of interventions.
frontier_candidates.main_risk: Dynamic optimization may introduce complexity that confuses human operators.
frontier_candidates.failure_value: Increased latency in paper generation without corresponding quality improvement.

frontier_candidates.title: Multi-Task Human Insight Integration
frontier_candidates.core_hypothesis: Integrating human insights across multiple research tasks will lead to a more coherent and impactful final manuscript.
frontier_candidates.why_now: Current systems often treat tasks in isolation; leveraging insights from various domains could enhance novelty and significance.
frontier_candidates.claim_it_tests: The impact of multi-task human insights on the coherence and quality of research outputs.
frontier_candidates.minimal_experiment: Run a series of experiments where human insights from different tasks are systematically integrated into the final paper.
frontier_candidates.benchmark_or_evaluator: Coherence and quality metrics based on expert evaluations.
frontier_candidates.human_taste_role: Humans will provide insights that guide the integration process across tasks.
frontier_candidates.main_risk: Overloading the system with too many insights may lead to confusion and reduced clarity.
frontier_candidates.failure_value: Decreased paper quality due to incoherent integration of insights.

frontier_candidates.title: Adaptive Experiment Budget Allocation
frontier_candidates.core_hypothesis: Implementing an adaptive budget allocation strategy for experiments based on real-time feedback will reduce wasted resources and improve research outcomes.
frontier_candidates.why_now: Current fixed budgets may not align with the evolving nature of research tasks; adaptive strategies can optimize resource use.
frontier_candidates.claim_it_tests: The effectiveness of adaptive budget allocation on resource efficiency and paper quality.
frontier_candidates.minimal_experiment: Conduct experiments with fixed vs. adaptive budgets to measure resource usage and paper quality.
frontier_candidates.benchmark_or_evaluator: Resource efficiency metrics and paper quality evaluations.
frontier_candidates.human_taste_role: Humans will provide feedback on the appropriateness of budget allocations and experimental directions.
frontier_candidates.main_risk: Adaptive strategies may lead to inconsistent experiment quality if not properly managed.
frontier_candidates.failure_value: Increased resource waste without corresponding improvements in research outcomes.

frontier_candidates.title: Structured Human Feedback Mechanism
frontier_candidates.core_hypothesis: Establishing a structured feedback mechanism for human input will enhance the reproducibility and clarity of research papers.
frontier_candidates.why_now: Current feedback is often informal and unstructured, leading to variability in paper quality; a structured approach could standardize improvements.
frontier_candidates.claim_it_tests: The impact of structured feedback on reproducibility and clarity metrics.
frontier_candidates.minimal_experiment: Implement a structured feedback process and compare the resulting manuscripts against those with informal feedback.
frontier_candidates.benchmark_or_evaluator: Reproducibility and clarity metrics based on expert evaluations.
frontier_candidates.human_taste_role: Humans will provide structured feedback using a predefined rubric.
frontier_candidates.main_risk: Over-structuring feedback may stifle creativity and lead to formulaic outputs.
frontier_candidates.failure_value: Reduced novelty and creativity in generated papers due to rigid feedback structures.

ranking.reason: Structured feedback mechanisms can significantly enhance reproducibility and clarity, with clear metrics for evaluation. The risk of stifling creativity is present but manageable.
Integrating human insights across tasks can improve coherence and impact. The potential for confusion exists, but the structured approach mitigates this risk.
Adaptive budget allocation is promising for resource efficiency but carries risks of inconsistent quality. The human role is less visible compared to other candidates.
Dynamic optimization introduces complexity that may confuse operators, leading to potential failures. The evidence gain is uncertain, and the human taste role is less defined.

critique.selection_rationale: The structured feedback mechanism offers the highest potential for reproducibility and clarity, with a well-defined experimental approach and metrics for evaluation.
critique.claim_boundary: The claims are bounded by the effectiveness of structured feedback in enhancing reproducibility and clarity, with a focus on measurable outcomes.

interpretation: Live AI Co-Scientist-style generate-critique-rank smoke for IGRE. This is hypothesis-frontier evidence and a protocol check, not a performance result or a human-selection result.
